svg.text: SELF-ORGANIZING MAPS
Reading the U-matrix: white = far from neighbours
the map from §4 (number = rows in the cell)
far
close
How a cell's shade is computed
Take the node's weight vector, measure the distance
to each of its (up to 8) grid neighbours, average,
divide by the map's largest average. Dense regions
of data: nodes packed close, dark. Gaps between
clusters, or lonely rows: nodes far apart, white.
What the red marks show
red outline = the 9 whitest cells, 20 rows flagged
red dot = cell holds a planted fraud (the truth
the course never has). Flags: 8 of 20 right (40%),
vs 2.9% at random. Not bad — but not fraud labels.
Then the course trains an ANN on the flags
Its labels are the SOM's guesses, so its accuracy
only measures agreement with the SOM (97.1% =
the score of "never fraud"). Its ranking found 2
true frauds in its top 20: worse than the flags.
white ≠ fraud: corner and edge nodes have fewer neighbours, and border cells between two clusters are white too
